name: Tessera Corponation Recursive Fold Microframe
description:
The Recursive Fold Microframe is a single-occupant personal vehicle engineered around a central design problem: how to move a person rapidly through GLMZ's dense urban environment and then make both the person and the vehicle disappear. The Microframe is a motorized two-wheeler in operational configuration, but its carbon-composite frame is built on a recursive folding joint system — a series of interlocking pivot points that allow the entire vehicle to collapse into a carry configuration roughly the size and shape of a large backpack in under eight seconds. The folded unit weighs 14 kg and is carried on an integrated harness. Deployment reverses the process: the rider drops the pack, catches the unfolding frame at hip height, and is in motion within twelve seconds of initiating deployment. The electric motor draws from a solid-state power cell integrated into the frame spine, providing a range of 60 km per charge at urban speeds.

The Microframe's performance in operational configuration is deliberately modest — a top speed of 55 km/h and an agility profile optimized for low-speed precision navigation through pedestrian-dense corridors rather than high-speed open transit. Its value is not in outrunning pursuit but in outmaneuvering it: the ability to enter a transit corridor on foot, deploy a vehicle in a moving crowd, transit to a secondary position, and fold back to foot-mobile before a response can be coordinated. Tessera Corponation's firmware includes a route-learning function that builds a personal map of the rider's habitual transit paths, optimizing folding and deployment point suggestions over time based on observed pursuit patterns and transit density data.

The Microframe was developed by Tessera Corponation's logistics research division as a last-mile delivery solution for high-density urban environments, but its adoption by GLMZ's runner and courier subculture was rapid and enthusiastic. Tessera Corponation has quietly leaned into this secondary market, offering a 'field edition' with reinforced joints, a reduced acoustic profile, and the route-learning firmware unlocked from its default corporate delivery parameters.

specifications.power_source: Integrated solid-state cell (frame spine), induction rechargeable
specifications.acoustic_signature: 22 dB at 5 meters (electric drivetrain, no exhaust)
specifications.firmware: Tessera Transit AI (route learning, deployment point optimization, pursuit pattern analysis)

tactical_use: The Microframe's primary tactical value is the transition between vehicle and foot-mobile states. A runner using a Microframe can enter a monitored zone on foot, deploy mid-transit to cover distance rapidly, fold before reaching a checkpoint or camera cluster, and continue on foot with no vehicle to search for or impound. The route-learning firmware actively improves this capability over time, identifying optimal fold and deploy points based on coverage gaps and pursuit response times. In courier operations, the Microframe is used for the final and most exposed segment of a run, where the ability to go vehicle-to-foot instantly is more valuable than raw speed.
cultural_context: The Recursive Fold Microframe has become a specific marker of the professional runner in GLMZ's courier culture — distinct from the amateur who rides a conventional bike or the corporate operative with an armored vehicle. Owning a Fold signals a certain level of operational sophistication: the understanding that disappearing is more valuable than speed. There is a ritual element to the fold and deploy sequence that experienced riders cultivate; the eight-second fold time is a benchmark that Microframe users practice and compare. The field edition's availability through semi-legitimate channels has made it accessible enough to be common in the Verge Corridors without being so common as to lose its professional association.
known_users: Professional courier runners in the Verge Corridors
Tessera Corponation last-mile delivery operators (corporate fleet)
Independent operatives requiring covert urban transit
Yuna Satch (courier, holds the current unofficial Verge Corridor fold-deploy record at 6.4 seconds)
Gray-market intelligence couriers moving physical data packages
Outer-ring organizers who need to transit between districts without leaving a vehicle trail
story_hooks: A Recursive Fold Microframe is recovered from a canal with its route-learning firmware intact. The routes stored in it map a series of locations across three districts that, connected, form a pattern nobody can immediately explain — but several of the locations are now crime scenes.

Tessera Corponation's route-learning firmware has been collecting anonymized transit data from all registered Microframes and feeding it to an undisclosed analytics system. Someone has obtained a partial data dump and is selling it — and the buyer list includes people who would use it to map runner transit patterns.

A Microframe user is leaving folded units at specific locations across the city as dead drops. The units are unregistered and the route-learning firmware has been wiped, but the carry harnesses all have the same custom modification. Someone is building a network and the player characters keep finding the nodes.

The field edition Microframe has a firmware vulnerability that allows an outside party to activate the route-learning system silently and transmit its data in real time. A Tessera Corponation insider is trying to quietly warn the runner community before the corporate security division realizes the warning is going out.

physical_description.visual_profile: A minimalist two-wheeler with an almost skeletal aesthetic when operational — exposed recursive pivot joints visible along the frame spine create a distinctive articulated silhouette. The handlebars are narrow and angled slightly forward; the seat is a single curved saddle positioned above the central frame column. When folded, the entire assembly compresses into a nested geometric form resembling a angular travel pack with a pronounced central spine ridge.
physical_description.dimensions: Operational: 165 cm length × 45 cm width × 85 cm height from ground to handlebars. Folded: 58 cm height × 42 cm width × 28 cm depth (backpack-like profile).
physical_description.weight_description: 14 kg folded and carried via integrated shoulder harness; handheld during the final stages of deployment/folding; light enough for sustained carry by a single person but requires deliberate handling during the fold/unfold transition.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite frame with visible joint articulation; polymer-wrapped handlebars; synthetic soft-touch saddle
physical_description.finish: Matte technical composite with a slight grip-texture coating; bare carbon weave visible at stress points and frame joints for visual authenticity; minimal gloss to reduce reflection signature
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with charcoal frame detailing; accent striping along the power-cell spine in deep Tessera corporate blue (#003366); matte black wheels and joints
physical_description.interface_elements: Small holographic deployment timer on the left handlebar (faintly illuminated, off when folded); minimal interface — a single power button on the frame spine (glowing pulse when charged); integrated induction charging port recessed into the rear of the seat column; simple LED battery indicator (three-stage: green/amber/red) visible when folded
distinctive_features: Recursive fold joints visible as interlocking chevron patterns along frame spine
Smooth geometric collapse of the frame during folding — no dangling straps or exposed wiring
Ultra-narrow profile when deployed — almost sideways-oriented aesthetic compared to traditional bikes
Integrated harness attachment points that lock flush with the frame when folded
Absence of pedals — pure electric, no hybrid mechanical option
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Corporation logo (minimalist Φ symbol) embossed on the seat column; 'Recursive Fold Microframe — Gen 4' stamped on the rear frame joint; Vasquez Biocompatible Materials microstamp on the carbon weave near the power cell; regulatory compliance markers (GLMZ Transit Authority approval) on the left frame spine
physical_description.condition_typical: Operational unit shows minor scuff marks on the frame from corridor navigation; small dust accumulation on the joint hinges; battery indicator glowing steady green. Folded configuration: harness straps snug and secure, frame locked in compressed state with no visible wobble or misalignment in the joints.
